title: Spectral norms in a scalar envelope inside the norm completion
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, $H=\widehat F$ its metric completion [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion], and $F\subseteq Q\subseteq H$ an intermediate field with the restricted absolute value. Let $E/F$ be a finite field extension with minimal-polynomial spectral norm $s=s_{E/F}$ [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. Let $\mathcal C$ be the metric completion of $(E,s)$, namely Cauchy sequences modulo sequences tending to zero, with norm $N([(e_j)])=\lim_j s(e_j)$. Termwise sums and products and multiplication by scalar Cauchy sequences make $\mathcal C$ a commutative $H$-algebra, and the canonical map $E\hookrightarrow\mathcal C$ is an isometric algebra embedding. Inside $\mathcal C$ put $M=\sum_{e\in E}Qe$, the set of finite $Q$-linear combinations of elements of $E$. Then $M$ is a finite-dimensional reduced commutative $Q$-algebra containing $E$. For $z\in M$, let $p_z(Z)=Z^r+\sum_{i=1}^r a_iZ^{r-i}$ be its monic polynomial of least positive degree annihilating $z$, and put $\sigma_{M/Q}(z)=\max_{1\le i\le r}|a_i|_Q^{1/i}$. The restriction of $N$ to $M$ is a definite, power-multiplicative nonarchimedean $Q$-algebra norm (in particular $N(qz)=|q|_Q N(z)$), and $$N(z)\le\sigma_{M/Q}(z)\quad(z\in M),\qquad \sigma_{M/Q}(e)=s_{E/F}(e)\quad(e\in E).$$ No weak stability, completeness of $F$ or $Q$, or separability of $E/F$ is assumed.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm], $s$ is a definite normalized ultrametric $F$-algebra norm; by [lem-trf-algebraic-spectral-norm-powers], $s(e^m)=s(e)^m$ for $m\ge1$. Apply [lem-trf-normed-algebra-completed-scalars] to $A=E$ and $n=s$. Its Cauchy quotient is exactly $\mathcal C$ in the statement, and supplies the asserted $H$-algebra, the isometric $F$-algebra embedding of $E$, and all the asserted norm identities. Restrict the scalar identity from $H$ to its subfield $Q$.

proof.text: Choose an $F$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $E$. Expanding elements of $E$ in this basis shows $M=\sum_{i=1}^dQe_i$. Each product $e_ie_j$ is an $F$-linear combination of the $e_k$, so multiplying two such $Q$-linear combinations stays in $M$; also $1\in E\subset M$. Thus $M$ is a finite-dimensional commutative unital $Q$-algebra. If $z^m=0$ for $m\ge1$, then $0=N(z^m)=N(z)^m$ and definiteness gives $z=0$, proving reducedness. The $d+1$ powers $1,z,\ldots,z^d$ are linearly dependent. A nonzero annihilating polynomial can be divided by its leading coefficient; a monic one of least degree exists. Its degree is positive because $1\ne0$ and $Q$ embeds in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Elementary scalar-span and polynomial arguments from the completed algebra and norm identities of step 1; comparison with spectralNorm at line 381.

proof.text: Write $p_z(Z)=Z^r+\sum_{i=1}^ra_iZ^{r-i}$. Suppose $t=N(z)>\sigma_{M/Q}(z)$. Then $t>0$ and $|a_i|_Qt^{r-i}<t^r$ for every $1\le i\le r$. The identities of step 1 give $N(a_iz^{r-i})=|a_i|_Qt^{r-i}$, including $r-i=0$ since $N(1)=1$. Iterating the strong triangle inequality over these $r\ge1$ terms gives $N(\sum_i a_iz^{r-i})<t^r$. But $p_z(z)=0$ identifies this sum with $-z^r$, whose norm is $t^r$, a contradiction. Hence $N(z)\le\sigma_{M/Q}(z)$. This argument uses only the explicit norm identities, so applies even though $M$ may have zero divisors.

proof.text: Fix $e\in E$, and let $f\in F[Z]$ and $g\in Q[Z]$ be its monic minimal polynomials over $F$ and in $M/Q$, respectively. Divide the coefficientwise image $f_Q$ by $g$. The remainder annihilates $e$; if nonzero, dividing by its leading coefficient contradicts the least degree of $g$. Thus $g\mid f_Q$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/Q$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Both polynomials split there by [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization]; their positive degrees give nonempty root multisets, and every root of $g$ is a root of $f_Q$ since $g\mid f_Q$. Give $\Omega$ its $Q$-spectral algebra norm by [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm], which has the positive-power property by [lem-trf-algebraic-spectral-norm-powers]. Apply [lem-trf-tate-root-spectral-formula] to each polynomial. Their spectral values are the maxima of this same norm on their roots, so $\sigma_{M/Q}(e)\le s_{E/F}(e)$: coefficient norms of $f_Q$ equal those of $f$. Conversely step 3 and the isometry of step 1 give $s_{E/F}(e)=N(e)\le\sigma_{M/Q}(e)$. This proves equality, including $e=0$ (then $f=g=Z$).
